description: Canonical structure for generated and evolved skills. Section names are stable machine IDs; headings are accepted Markdown headings; aliases preserve older goal files.

sections.name: overview
sections.description: What the skill accomplishes and the scope it owns.

sections.name: when_to_use
sections.description: Positive invocation conditions and recognizable triggers.

sections.name: do_not_use
sections.description: Negative invocation boundaries; this is distinct from execution constraints.
headings: Do not use this skill when

sections.name: workflow
sections.description: The methodology, procedure, or ordered process used to perform the work.

sections.name: constraints
sections.description: Rules, invariants, safety boundaries, and conditions that apply during execution.

sections.name: verification
sections.description: Checks, acceptance criteria, and evidence required before the work is complete.

sections.name: output_format
sections.description: The required structure, fields, files, or presentation of the result.

sections.name: limitations
sections.description: Known capability limits, assumptions, and unsupported cases.

sections.name: state_machine
sections.description: Optional states, transitions, retries, and terminal conditions for stateful workflows.

sections.name: examples
sections.description: Optional representative inputs, decisions, and outputs.

sections.name: prerequisites
sections.description: Optional setup, dependencies, permissions, and required context.

sections.name: best_practices
sections.description: Optional recommendations that improve quality but are not hard constraints.

sections.name: other
sections.description: A named heading outside the current vocabulary.

dirs.name: references
dirs.description: Supporting documentation and source material loaded when needed.

dirs.name: assets
dirs.description: Static files used or emitted by the skill.

dirs.name: evals
dirs.description: Evaluation fixtures, cases, and expected outcomes.

dirs.name: other
dirs.description: A named directory outside the current vocabulary.
